correctness.rationale: Every nonhub-positive-indegree orientation on a petal is exactly +^a-^(ell-a), with ell-1 outward and two cyclic directions. At least one cyclic petal is necessary to feed the hub. Hub and internal predecessors are forced: outward contribution ell-3, cyclic ell-2, and one extra terminal cyclic predecessor dominates hub; score b+c, b=2+sum(ell_i-3), c>=1 cyclic petals. Product of (ell_i-1+2z) minus all-outward yields A(z). For each noncyclic petal there are two endpoint-orientation unique choices and ell-3 interior orientations with two choices; weighted factor 2(ell_i-2). Cyclic factor2z times c choices to dominate hub, giving T=z^b z d/dz product(2(ell_i-2)+2z). Direct independently written orientation/subset brute-force matches both polynomials on several multi-petal graphs; infinite proof is the local decomposition.
